<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Sp1nd01" />{{rh|Gods promiſe.|Geneſis|Abrams viſion.}} {{rule}} <!-- useful info for KJV Common characters: ſ ¶ ⁊ ⸗ <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Note text''}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Note text}} ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Note text''}}  Remember that v and u are combined, "v" appears at beginnings of words and "u" in the middle Remember that i and j are combined, use "i" or "I" in all cases.--></noinclude>take the goods to thy ſelfe.

{{verse|14|22}}And Abram ſaid to the King of Sodome, I haue lift vp my hand vnto the LORD, the moſt high God, the poſſeſſour of heauen and earth,

{{verse|14|23}}That I wil not take from a threed euen to a ſhoe latchet, and that I will not take any thing that is thine, leſt thou ſhouldeſt ſay, I haue made Abram rich:

{{verse|14|24}}Saue onely that which the yong men haue eaten, and the portion of the men which went with mee, Aner, Eſchol, and Mamre; let them take their portion.

==={{Chapter|15|CHAP. XV.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#15:1|1]] God encourageth Abram. [[#15:2|2]] Abram complaineth for want of an heire. [[#15:4|4]] God promiſeth him a ſonne, and a multiplying of his ſeed. [[#15:6|6]] Abram is iuſtified by faith. [[#15:7|7]] Canaan is promiſed againe, and confirmed by a ſigne, [[#15:12|12]] and a viſion.}}

{{Verse|15|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|A|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2v (A).png|imgsize=100px}}Fter theſe things, the word of the LORD came vnto Abram in a viſion, ſaying; Feare not, Abram: I am thy ſhield, {{smaller|and}} thy exceeding *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Pſal.16.16.}} great reward.

{{verse|15|2}}And Abram ſaid, Lord GOD, what wilt thou giue me, ſeeing I goe childleſſe? and the ſteward of my houſe {{smaller|is}} this Eliezer of Damaſcus.

{{verse|15|3}}And Abram ſaid; Behold, to mee thou haſt giuen no ſeed: and loe, one borne in my houſe is mine heire.

{{verse|15|4}}And behold, the word of the LORD {{smaller|came}} vnto him, ſaying; This ſhall not be thine heire: but he that ſhall come foorth out of thy owne bowels, ſhalbe thine heire.

{{verse|15|5}}And he brought him forth abroad, and ſaid, Looke now towards heauen, and tell the ſtarres, if thou be able to number them. And hee ſaid vnto him, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Rom.4.18.}} So ſhall thy ſeed be.

{{verse|15|6}}And he *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Rom.4.3. galat.3.6. iam.2.23.}} beleeued in the LORD; and hee counted it to him for righteouſneſſe.

{{verse|15|7}}And he ſaid vnto him; I am the LORD that brought thee out of Ur of the Caldees, to giue thee this land, to inherit it.

{{verse|15|8}}And he ſaid, Lord GOD, whereby ſhal I know that I ſhall inherit it?

{{verse|15|9}}And he ſaid vnto him, Take me an heifer of three yeeres old, and a ſhee goat of three yeeres old, and a ramme of three yeeres old, and a turtle doue, and a yong pigeon.

{{verse|15|10}}And he tooke vnto him all theſe, and diuided them in the midſt, and layd each peece one againſt another: but the birds diuided he not.

{{verse|15|11}}And when the fowles came downe vpon the carcaſes, Abram droue them away.

{{verse|15|12}}And when the Sunne was going downe, a deepe ſleepe fell vpon Abram: and loe, an horrour of great darkeneſſe fell vpon him.

{{verse|15|13}}And he ſaid vnto Abram, Know of a ſurety, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Acts.7.6.}} that they ſeed ſhalbe a ſtranger, in a land that is not theirs, and ſhal ſerue them, and they ſhall afflict them foure hundred yeeres.

{{verse|15|14}}And alſo that nation whom they ſhall ſerue, wil I iudge: and afterward ſhall they come out with great ſubſtance.

{{verse|15|15}}And thou ſhalt goe to thy fathers in peace; thou ſhalt be buried in a good old age.

{{verse|15|16}}But in the fourth generation they ſhall come hither againe: for the iniquitie of the Amorites is not yet full.

{{verse|15|17}}And it came to paſſe that when the Sunne went downe, and it was {{smaller|darke}}, behold, a ſmoking furnace, and a <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebrewe. a lampe of fire.''}} burning lampe that paſſed betweene thoſe pieces.

{{verse|15|18}}In that ſame day the LORD made a couenant with Abram, ſaying; *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chap.12.7. and 13.15. & 26.4. deut.34.4.}} Vnto thy ſeed haue I giuen this land from the riuer of Egypt vnto the great riuer, the riuer Euphrates:

{{verse|15|19}}The Kenites, and the Kenizites, and the Kadmonites:

{{verse|15|20}}And the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Rephaims,

{{verse|15|21}}And the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgaſhites, and the Iebuſites.

==={{Chapter|16|CHAP. XVI.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#16:1|1]] Sarai, being barren, giueth Hagar to Abram. [[#16:4|4]] Hagar being afflicted for deſpiſing her miſtreſſe, runneth away. [[#16:7|7]] An Angel ſendeth her backe to ſubmit her ſelfe, [[#16:11|11]] and telleth her of her child. [[#16:15|15]] Iſmael is borne.}}

{{Verse|16|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|N|image=King James Bible (1611) page A4r (N).png|imgsize=100px}}Ow Sarai Abrams wife bare him no children: and ſhe had an handmaide, an Egyptian, whoſe name was Hagar.

{{verse|16|2}}And Sarai ſaid vnto Abram, Behold now, the LORD hath reſtrained me from bearing: I pray thee go in vnto my maid: it may bee that I may<noinclude>{{right|<sup>†</sup> obtaine}}</noinclude>
